name: tmem_pipeline
purpose: Separate UTCCP completion, independent-copy throughput, same-SM contention and copy-to-MMA ordering. No workload timing is used to derive a value.

attribution_before_data.code: BlackwellModule::on_instance_issue(kSemaTmemCopy) only updates sttm_until_; umma_commit consults umma_done_ only, and umma_issue reserves tensor_pipe_start only for MMA. Thus a copy-only commit ignores prior copies. Whether omitted copy service also explains the block-scaled workload delay is a hypothesis, not a conclusion.
attribution_before_data.isa: NVIDIA PTX ISA, https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html, sections Pipelined tcgen05 Instructions and mbarrier based completion mechanism: commit tracks same-thread prior mma/cp/shift; same-warp cp-to-mma operand ordering has qualifier/address restrictions. Do not serialize every unrelated tcgen05 operation based merely on its name.
attribution_before_data.captured_path: $A/fg-gemm/jr10/bw-fg/CUF-DSL-BS-NVF4-V16-R05/facts/000273.gsc: warp 4 executes eight UTCCP.T.S.4x32dp128bit followed by four UTCOMMA.BLOCK16 and UTCBAR per inner group, 27 groups in this cluster. This confirms the candidate path executes, not its hardware timing.
attribution_before_data.existing_copy_evidence: mechtree.w1.tmem.copy.cta_group.1 measured 42.4716796875 cycles for PTX 32x128b.warpx4; the old same-destination U-series means give about 42.94 cycles/copy, but this is not proof of independent-copy service. The current instruction.service UTCCP interval is structural zero.

probe.structure: One CTA of 128 threads. One or two producer/detector pairs, producer warps 0/2 and detector warps 1/3, all on the same SM. Distinct producer TMEM destinations and barriers. Reuse tensor_pipe_forms helpers for allocation, descriptor construction, elected issue, jitter and test_wait detection. 512 allocated columns; D at columns 0/128, copy/scales at 256/384. Source A/B all FP4 ones, scales all E4M3 ones.
probe.copies: PTX tcgen05.cp.cta_group::1.32x128b.warpx4 (expected UTCCP.T.S.4x32dp128bit). U=0,1,2,4,8,16,32; independent destinations advance by four TMEM columns, do not overlap, and remain below column 512. Same-destination U=1..32 is a historical diagnostic only, never a service-leaf source.
probe.mma: After the copies, zero, one or four elected m128n128k64 NVF4 block16 MMA operations on one accumulator per producer. U=0 provides empty-commit and pure-MMA controls. Copy destination zero contains the MMA's A scale factors; B scale factors start four columns later.
probe.measurement: Two runs; 16 launches per cell, 129 repetitions each, discard repetition zero. Producer delays by the existing jitter function, reads clock, issues U copies and M MMA, commits, writes its start timestamp, then waits for detector acknowledgement. Detector test_wait-spins, records clock and acknowledges. Retain each producer's duration and joint max(end)-min(start) for two-producer contention.
probe.value_check: Before timing each cell run reps=1. Initially clear the copied A-scale columns for U>0 (pure-copy cells also clear for U=0), leaving B scales equal to one. For U>0 the copy must restore the A scales; after MMA expect exactly 64*M in F32, otherwise expect copied bits 0x38383838 (U>0) or zero (U=0). Check after every launch. A timeout, bad value or CUDA error invalidates the cell.

sass_gate: All 54 template kernels must be present. Exactly U UTCCP of the specified form and M UTCOMMA.BLOCK16, one UTCBAR after the targets. No BRA/ELECT/WARPSYNC between first and last target, and no LDC/LDCU/ULDC/LDG/STG in that interval. Record the last CLOCKLO before targets/commit, start-to-first-target SASS stall sum, and the target instruction list. Zero matches or unexpected copies/MMA fail; no silent form substitution.

derivation.samples: Mean of retained elapsed cycles per cell and observer, because the cross-warp jitter averages the detector grid; retain median and P10/P90 as diagnostics. Correct only start-to-first-target overhead using each compiled kernel's SASS stalls relative to U=0 empty commit.
derivation.copy: For rotated, one-producer copy-only cells, fit elapsed versus U in {1,2,4,8,16,32} by ordinary least squares. Report slope, intercept, each residual, single-copy-minus-empty-commit and two-run agreement. Same-destination slopes are diagnostic only. Two producers test the predicted shared-service envelope; do not call a per-warp issue interval an SM service rate without this evidence.
derivation.mixture: Report E(U,M)-E(0,M), the independent-copy prediction U*copy_slope and the copy-only increment. Different predictions for overlap and serialization remain explicit. A model change requires interpreting the measured mixed sequence and ISA dependencies, not just choosing whichever improves full-gpu MAPE.

acceptance: SASS and value checks first. Existing single-copy latency control within max(5 cycles,15%) of 42.47 after clock-prefix correction, both runs within max(2 cycles,5%); independent-copy OLS residual within max(4 cycles,5% of elapsed). If any fails, report the raw evidence and cause before a post-data addendum. No new model or leaf is authorized by this protocol alone.
scope: cta_group::1 only in this first experiment; no extrapolation to 2CTA or other copy shapes. Completion tracking required by ISA is distinct from an empirically calibrated copy service resource.
validation_after_any_change: Focused semantic CTest and replay of these same binaries/captures; strict tree validation for leaf changes; full H100 and B300 regression with r17 cases/references unchanged. Preserve missing-fact rejection. Target each architecture full-gpu MAPE<5%, P90<10%; single-cluster accuracy is diagnostic only.

addenda.reason: The checker first failed on the parser API (Kernel.insts, not an iterable Kernel). After that interface fix, 54 kernels were found and only cp2.mma4.rot1.p1 failed: ptxas moved the start-timestamp STG between UTCCP and UTCOMMA. No hardware timing cells were run.
addenda.change: Publish the producer start timestamp after the acknowledgement wait, with a membar.cta before the publication to prevent hoisting that store into the timed operations. The detector has already captured its end timestamp before acknowledging. This adds work outside the measured interval and before the next jitter delay. Same SASS rejection and numerical criteria; rebuild in b300-r2 rather than overwriting r1.

addenda.observed: Both runs: single-producer independent-copy slope 8.547 cycles/copy, corrected single-copy-minus-empty 9.66, so the old 42.47 latency control FAILS. Same and rotated destinations agree. Two-producer joint windows range roughly 418..697 cycles for the copy-only series, with large nonmonotonic residuals. The independent producer loops accumulate different iteration-start offsets, so pairing their repetition indexes does not bound concurrent work.
addenda.old_control_attribution: Read-only inspection of /path/to/blackwell-prototype/artifacts/mechtree/w1r4-a/out/sass/tmem_alloc_cp.sass (the exact run cited by leaf_values_umma.json): k_cp<1,4,0,1> has ELECT at 0xb80, UTCCP at 0xb90, three control instructions including BRA.U.ANY through 0xbc0, and another elected wrapper for UTCBAR. The original derivation subtracts only the clock-to-first-copy prefix, so the post-copy elected wrapper remains in 42.47. This is not a pure intrinsic copy-completion control. It must remain recorded as failed, not be used to force the new measurement to 42.47.
addenda.change: All 128 threads now execute one outer repetition loop, with __syncthreads before each repetition. Producers and detectors retain their existing roles inside it. The barrier is before jitter and measured start clocks. This prevents accumulated repetition-index skew; inspect joint versus individual windows and pairwise start skew in r3 before inferring SM sharing.
addenda.acceptance_change: Remove the requirement to reproduce the contaminated historical 42.47 value as a prerequisite for a new physical service value; retain it as a failed historical control with the SASS attribution above. Keep the existing SASS gate, exact value checks, OLS residual and two-run agreement bounds. Pure-MMA control E(0,1)-E(0,0), prefix corrected, must reproduce the independently installed beat+completion (64+56.75 cycles) within max(5 cycles,10%). No model is installed by this addendum.

addenda.observed: Aligned epochs give start skew zero in the retained r3 samples. Independent-copy slopes: one producer 8.3727793 cycles/copy, two producers joint 17.0366999 cycles/copy. The pure-MMA single-op increment is 117.68 versus the installed 120.75, and satisfies the replacement control. These establish SM-shared copy service, but symmetric copy-then-MMA cells do not distinguish a shared copy/MMA execution port from separate ports with operand dependencies.
addenda.new_cells: Add split=1 cells, one CTA and two producer/detector pairs: producer 0 performs only U copies, producer 1 performs only M MMA, at disjoint TMEM addresses, both followed by their own commit. U={0,8,16,32}, M={0,1,4}; 12 additional kernels, including empty and single-operation-family controls. Producer 1's scales remain preinitialized and do not depend on producer 0's copies. All existing 54 symmetric cells are retained; total 66 kernels and 171 result rows per run.
addenda.sass_and_analysis: For split cells, check CP and MMA blocks separately for forbidden instructions: a branch between the two mutually exclusive producer paths is necessary and is not a within-path branch. Exactly U CP, M MMA and one common commit remain required. Do not apply a linear PC-range prefix subtraction across those mutually exclusive paths; split corrected_mean is explicitly null and only raw matched-control differences are used. The normal-cell gate and derivation are unchanged.
addenda.discriminator: At U=32 and M=4, each producer's service is about 256 cycles. Independent execution ports predict the joint elapsed near the slower standalone control; a shared service resource predicts roughly the sum of CP and MMA service plus one completion/detector tail. Compare both individual observers and joint clocks against the matched split U=0/M=0 controls. Do not infer shared-port ownership from the symmetric-cell improvement alone.

addenda.observed: For disjoint producer operands, the copy observer at U=32 rises from 432.448 to 691.219 cycles when the other producer executes four MMA: +258.771 versus four independently measured 64-cycle MMA beats. At U=16 the increase is +255.576. This discriminates shared copy/MMA service from independent ports with only same-address operand ordering. The existing one-producer versus two-producer copy result also supports shared service.
addenda.scope_extension: Before installation, measure cta_group::2 rather than extrapolating group 1, and independently measure all five PTX copy forms supported by the inherited compiler probe. Group 2 uses a two-CTA cluster, group-2 allocation/copy/MMA/commit, m=256 (128 rows per CTA), and rank 0 issuers/detectors. Both CTAs initialize operands/scales before a cluster barrier; another cluster barrier precedes readback/deallocation. Matching mbarriers exist on both ranks for the existing helper's multicast commit.
addenda.cells: Repeat all 66 group-1 kernels in group 2. Additionally, for each group, copy-only elected one-producer independent-address U=0,1,2,4,8,16 for shapes 128x256b, 4x256b, 128x128b, 64x128b.warpx2::02_13. Shape-4 32x128b.warpx4 keeps its earlier U=0..32 series and mixed/contended cells. Other forms advance destinations by eight columns, so none overlaps or exceeds allocated columns. Total 180 kernels and 438 result rows per run, 2048 samples per row. No new full-workload measurements select these cells.
addenda.compiler_coverage: The exact legacy w1r4-a tmem_alloc_cp.sass has the complete five forms in both groups: bare UTCCP.T.S (PTX 128x256b), .4dp256bit, .128dp128bit, .2x64dp128bit_lw02_lw13, .4x32dp128bit, with .2CTA where applicable. The checker now requires the precise selected spelling and group; it does not treat all shapes as x1.
addenda.derivation_and_limits: Same predeclared per-cell means, clock-prefix correction and per-form U-series OLS. Shape 4 has same-SM sharing evidence; other forms' scalar service rates are measured independently, not filled from neighboring forms. Report completion-minus-service residuals and their uncertainty before assigning any extra tail. No value from r5 is installed until the lead reviews the data and the proposed engine ownership.

addenda.review: All ten independent-address form/group OLS fits meet the unchanged residual and repeatability bounds. Single-copy-minus-service residuals range from -2.986 to +1.301 cycles, below the five-cycle resolution criterion; no separate positive tail is identifiable. Approved exact fit values, identities and diagnostic residuals are frozen in microbench/tmem_pipeline/b300-r5/calibration.json. install.py reads that capture, not a fresh derivation.
addenda.candidate_engine_rule: blackwell.tmem.copy cycles becomes full shared-SM tensor service, selected by cta_group and exact native tmem_shape. Copy reserves the existing tensor service frontier and enters the warp's commit completion set. UTCBAR enters after the prior shared service frontier, then waits for its own tracked completions and adds the existing commit latency. Existing STTM wait bookkeeping is unchanged in this scoped correction. Preserve fractional copy service in the SM frontier; round observable start/completion events up to integer cycles. Integer-only pipe reservations retain their previous start/finish values and Hopper is unchanged. Blackwell commit can change even without copies if another warp has earlier queued MMA service, as the foreign-commit fixture explicitly tests.
addenda.verification_before_full_gpu: Synthetic tests: copy-only commit cannot release early; two warps' copies serialize on the same SM but not different SMs; copy and MMA delay each other through shared service; an empty commit behind another warp's queued MMA cannot bypass the frontier; fractional copies accumulate rather than truncating each instruction. Converter tests cover all ten compiler-derived group/form spellings and reject unknown forms, while LDTM/STTM axes are unchanged. Replay existing r5 binaries through capture/convert/build/sim before accepting model precision. Treat any replay discrepancy as evidence to investigate, not a reason to adjust the ten frozen service rates.

addenda.before_replay_data: engine candidate 3033bf4a; hardware data remain the frozen b300-r5 measurement.json
addenda.selection: 48 cells: both CTA groups, normal shape-4 P=1/2, U=0/8/32, M=0/4 (24); split shape-4 U=0/32, M=0/4 (8); other four copy forms P=1,U=0/16,M=0 (16). The two U8/M4/P2 group-1/group-2 cells are structural pilots before the rest. No full-GPU error is used in this selection.
addenda.capture: Reuse the r5 binary, exact --only selection, one retained launch with 17 repetitions after the one-repetition value-check launch. Capture trace and placement for kernel occurrence 2. The instrumented program's timestamps are not hardware references. Replay clocks use journal issue times at the producer start CLOCKLO and detector end CLOCKLO, identified from the frozen SASS; jitter CLOCKLO reads are excluded. Drop repetition zero, retain 16 windows per observer. Require one cluster, correct actual cluster shape/rank, 17 clocks per actor and exact copy/MMA counts.
addenda.comparison: Before uses the r17 tree plus the unchanged r17 engine; after uses 3033bf4a tree/engine. Read the already-frozen uninstrumented hardware means, prefix corrections and diagnostics, never refit the service rates. Compare per-observer windows and matching U=0 increments, separately for raw split paths and prefix-corrected normal paths. The recorded 2032000-kHz device clock is passed explicitly; no invented whole-kernel reference time or cache-control observation is supplied. Warmup/jitter and trace-dependent polling can change the detector phase distribution, so report those residuals instead of adjusting a leaf.
addenda.storage: Keep traces, jobs and journals for this bounded replay. The current /data free space is below the 150-GB full-suite start line, so full-card regression remains pending; no old evidence is deleted.

addenda.observed_failure: Both pilot captures succeeded, but the first job build rejected missing_fact:reference_cache_control (launch.json). Unprofiled r5 did not observe a cache-control setting, and the engine intentionally rejects unknown or none. The failed build and its facts are retained; no all/default fact is inserted.
addenda.resolution: reference.py invokes the existing NCU reference runner with its explicit --cache-control all and --clock-control none. It profiles the unchanged r5 binary, exact selected variants, one value-check launch plus a 17-repetition launch. Match the actual traced (kernel, occurrence=2) via the existing census_row helper and require identical grid/block/cluster dimensions. Record real cycles and clock metrics, NCU CSV and program timer output. Pass this real reference TSV into both replay arms rather than supplying a fabricated time or forcing the cache flag.
addenda.limits: The ten service rates and r5 hardware window comparisons are unchanged. Newly observed cold-reference timer samples are retained as a separate diagnostic; they do not refit the leaf. The engine clock now comes from the matched NCU reference, not the nominal device clock override. Any difference from the earlier unprofiled windows must be reported, not silently relabelled.

addenda.after_replay_execution: All 48 cells and both engine arms completed, but aggregate extraction first failed at before/cp0.mma4.rot1.p2.split.
addenda.reader_correction: The reader counted the operation class without distinguishing predicated-off issues. Direct job inspection confirms warp 0 has 68 UTCOMMA issue records with semantics=NONE (four predicated-off operations per repetition), whereas warp 2 has 68 actual kind-23 MMA operations. Count executed copies/MMA by their kind-30/kind-23 semantic rows and report predicated-off issues separately. Keep exact 17*U / 17*M executed-count assertions. This changes only extraction; do not recapture, reconvert, resimulate or refit hardware values.

addenda.after_semantic_count_check: Both CTA groups' U16/M0/P1 shape-3 copies have active_mask=predicate_mask=1 in capture facts, but no semantic rows in either replay arm.
addenda.cause: The older Python/C++ tmem_shape_repeat semantic parsers do not recognize native 2x64dp128bit_lw02_lw13, despite its new timing axis being recognized. Each affected launch.json explicitly records 272 unsupported:tmem_shape errors. The converter can emit diagnostic partial segments with exit zero; the standard batch wrapper rejects their missing_facts/unsupported maps, but this replay recipe omitted those checks.
addenda.repair: Add the exact native semantic spelling with the existing copy (N<<16)|M encoding, and cover all ten form/group combinations plus predicated-off operations in both segment builders. Check both capture-facts and segment launch.json diagnostic maps before building/simulating, and check them again before extracting windows. Preserve the four invalid arm/cell outputs and rerun conversion/build/simulation only for the two affected cells; no capture, NCU measurement or calibrated value changes. Other 46 cells' diagnostic maps are empty.
addenda.additional_parity_fix: The new builder tests also expose a Python Blackwell-only decode omission: the architecture decoder did not skip predicated-off instructions, unlike C++ decode_semantics and Python's common decoder. Add the same active_mask & predicate_mask guard before architecture dispatch. The six new tests pass: both builders and both CTA groups cover all five native copies plus inactive copies, and inactive UMA/commit need no operand facts. Hopper and C++ predication behavior are unchanged.

addenda.replay_outcome: All 48 cells x both engine arms now have complete diagnostics-free jobs and validated executed-instruction counts; repair and extraction exit 0. Results are frozen at fg-gemm/tmem-pipeline-replay/measurement.json and comparison.json under the external artifact root. Only the two affected shape-3 cells were rebuilt from preserved facts; all failed outputs and both hardware-reference sets remain.
addenda.copy_only: Across 12 positive-U, M=0, one-producer contrasts covering all five forms and both CTA groups, the maximum error in baseline- and prefix-corrected copy increments is 4.2744140625 cycles. Do not change the ten frozen service rates to compensate for other errors.
addenda.mixed_counterexamples: For split U32/M4 versus U32/M0, the model adds 256 cycles to copy completion in both CTA groups. Frozen r5 hardware adds 258.7705078125 (group 1) and 154.68310546875 (group 2); the separate 16-sample cold reference adds 224 and 136.1875. Conversely, copy's effect on the MMA producer is modeled as +130/+131 cycles but r5 shows +15.79296875/-62.51708984375 (cold: +22.25/-105.3125). Group-2 mixed joint completion is predicted at 720 versus 597.796875 cycles. These are retained counterexamples, not a reason to refit copy throughput.
addenda.limits: Copy-only replay supports the measured copy service, but does not validate treating the entire MMA initiation interval as exclusive shared-copy service. Front-end admission, queue capacity, operand-path sharing, and commit ordering remain alternative explanations. Group-2 empty-commit absolute windows are also about 23 cycles high. No post-change full-card accuracy result exists; r17 remains the acceptance baseline, and /data remains at 103GB below the 150GB start line.

addenda.next_experiment_design_pending_implement: Distinguish admission timing from completion interference without changing the r5 binary or calibration. Proposed separate admission.cu: two producer/detector pairs, independent copy and MMA operands, U=0/32, M=0/4, CTA group=1/2, MMA A source=SMEM/TMEM, N=64/128, M-dimension=128*CTA-group, K=64. The ordinary role mapping gives 32 cells; add the eight AS=SMEM,N=128 controls with producer roles swapped between warp 0 and warp 2, total 40 cells.
addenda.planned_observations: Add one producer CLOCKLO immediately after its target body and before commit. Publish start/admission timestamps only after acknowledgment, preserving the existing detector endpoint. Retain raw per-producer admission and completion samples, joint completion, start skew, and warp-slot observations outside the timed window. Run two independent 16-launch x129-repetition measurements, dropping repetition zero, after a value-check launch. These are diagnostic contrasts, not new fitted service rates.
addenda.planned_layout_and_checks: Reuse existing umma_impl.cuh and its verified 32-column TMEM A fill with 0x22222222 at columns 0..31. MMA D uses 128..255, independent copy destinations 256..383, and MMA scale factors 384..511. Preserve r5's padded SMEM descriptors to avoid changing bank layout during N/source comparisons. Clear the full copy destination region before timing, then check its first/last columns on both CTAs (zero for U0, 0x38383838 for U32). Check MMA values on both CTAs and at the first/last N columns. SASS validation must check all 40 cells, target counts/forms/CTA group/A source, no wrapper within target spans, and producer start/admission clocks before commit plus detector clock after it.
addenda.architectural_reference: PTX ISA section tcgen05.cp, https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#tcgen05-instructions-tcgen05-cp, inspected directly: cta_group::2 causes both current and peer CTA to copy from their own shared memory into Tensor Memory. Thus peer-copy value checking is required for the proposed probe. Current documentation also lists warpx2::01_23 and decompression forms; they are not among the five measured forms and remain unsupported by this calibration. Do not infer their timing or claim that five measured forms exhaust every compiler/version's native forms.
addenda.planned_analysis: For each source/N/group/role mapping, compare mixed against copy-only on the copy observer and against MMA-only on the MMA observer, separately for admission and completion intervals. Negative interference is evidence and must not be clipped. Source/N sensitivity after accounting for admission can discriminate operand-resource sharing from whole-tensor serialization; role-swap sensitivity can expose arbitration. Large start skew is a confound to explain, not a missing value to fill. Author the new CUDA probe, structural checker and numerical analysis before execution; do not delegate their design or use full-card errors to choose parameters.
addenda.first_step_narrowed_before_measurement: Do not launch the proposed 40-cell source/N/role matrix yet. First obtain direct admission evidence for only the eight existing split contrasts: U0/32 x M0/4 x CTA-group1/2, AS=SMEM, N=128, ordinary roles. admission.cu and check_admission.py implement this bounded instrumentation step. The extra producer clock separates issue/admission from completion; both-CTA first/last-column value checks and warp-slot observations strengthen correctness. Run two 16-launch x129-repetition collections with seed bases 0 and 64, and inspect source/SASS plus these observations before selecting any further perturbation. No new leaf or engine change is authorized by an aggregate fit.
addenda.phase_sampling_note: The retained r5 run-a and run-b are distinct files with distinct UTC fields but all 438 raw sample arrays are identical; their fixed launch seeds repeat the same phase schedule. Preserve both, but do not count them as independent phase coverage. The admission probe records seed_base and uses non-overlapping launch-seed ranges 1..16 and 65..80. This changes the new diagnostic experiment only; do not recompute or refit r5 calibration.

addenda.admission_execution: Eight kernels pass SASS checks and both 16x129 collections pass all values, including peer-CTA first/last columns. nvcc 13.2.78, B300 SXM6 AC GPU-44b3fe27-b778-d401-7d04-0cc8615235cc on gpu-b300-1302, driver 580.159.03. The initial -arch=sm_103a invocation failed at PTX assembly; explicit -gencode arch=compute_103a,code=sm_103a succeeded. Both attempts remain under fg-gemm/tmem-admission, with measurements in measurement.json and placement-observations.json. Exit-explicit is zero.
addenda.admission_observation: With M=0, U32's producer interval is 269.84/270.04 cycles for group 1 and 165.91/165.78 for group 2; pure M4's interval is 30 cycles in both groups. Mixed U32/M4 increases the copy producer interval by 263.35/263.31 cycles (group 1) and 167.71/168.04 (group 2). The group-2 negative MMA completion contrast persists (-53.23/-48.39 cycles). Starts are aligned in every sample. Each observed warp-slot pair (0,2),(1,3),(2,0),(3,1) occurs four times per run and the qualitative effects persist in each pair.
addenda.source_observation: SASS copies cycle through read-barrier IDs 0..5 with no explicit wait masks in the body. The admission CLOCKLO also has no wait mask; R2UR immediately afterward waits on mask 0x3f before UTCBAR. Current Simulator::issue resets read barriers at issue except for existing MIO/L1 acceptance paths; Blackwell copy/MMA callbacks do not extend them to tensor acceptance, and instance_ready has no copy-specific admission capacity. This identifies missing modeled paths, not a measured release latency or queue capacity.
addenda.next_short_burst_before_measurement: Add only U8/M0 for CTA groups 1 and 2 to distinguish short-burst admission from the existing U32 observations. Keep all eight original outputs frozen and run only the two new variants, using seeds 0/64 and 16x129 again. The checker now covers ten compiled kernels. Value checks use the first and last written copy columns (31 for U8, 127 for U32); no other numeric or timing change. Compare against frozen U0/U32 and inspect each SASS prefix; do not infer an exact capacity from U32 alone or launch the deferred source/N/role matrix.

addenda.short_burst_execution: Ten compiled kernels pass SASS validation. The first execution recipe reused each output directory across two --only processes; MbWriter uses fopen(w), so group 2 overwrote the newly collected group-1 records. This loss was reported, surviving group-2 files were retained, and only group 1 was recollected under short-burst/cg1. Both seed cohorts now contain all six required observer records across the two directory roots, with no value failures. All collections used the same GPU-44b3fe27 as the first admission experiment.
addenda.short_burst_observation: U8 copy admission is 61.0 cycles in both seed cohorts for group 1 and 55.01513671875/55.02294921875 for group 2. SASS prefix stalls from start CLOCKLO to first UTCCP sum to 29 and tail stalls from last UTCCP to admission CLOCKLO sum to 2, for both U8 and U32 in both groups; all target control stalls are 1. These facts do not by themselves establish an exact queue capacity. Frozen summary: fg-gemm/tmem-admission/short-burst-measurement.json (parent directory used because the pod-owned child is not writable on ).
addenda.next_investigation: Inspect the existing SASS patch infrastructure before any new measurement. A narrowly scoped candidate is to strengthen only the admission CLOCKLO's wait mask to 0x3f, which the following R2UR already waits on, to observe source-read barrier completion separately from issue admission. This must preserve all target instructions and other control bits, retain the original binary, validate exact patched locations and values, and not weaken any dependency. No patch or new experiment has yet been executed. Do not install guessed capacities or release latencies, and do not expand the deferred source/N/role matrix without discriminating evidence.

addenda.read_wait_experiment_before_measurement: The active tree has no reusable cubin patcher. The existing short-burst executable contains uncompressed CUDA ELF64 sections, so patch_admission_wait.py uses the existing sass_ctrl parser plus standard-library ELF section reads. It validates every decoded instruction against the binary, creates a new executable, and changes only the wait-mask bits of four admission CS2R instructions: U8/32, M0, CTA groups 1/2. Each selected clock originally has wait mask zero and is immediately followed by R2UR waiting on 0x3f. The patch sets the clock's wait mask to 0x3f; every other byte except the corresponding eight bytes across the four words must remain unchanged.
addenda.read_wait_validation: Run patch, disassemble the new executable, and run verify to compare all ten kernels. All instructions, registers, target counts and control bits other than those four wait masks must match. Execute only the four selected cells, two seed cohorts 0/64 and 16x129 each, retaining all existing value checks. Use a separate output directory for every cell and run to prevent MbWriter truncation. Reuse frozen native measurements rather than rerun them; record actual GPU identity and qualify any cross-device contrast. A read-wait timestamp measures scoreboard release, not necessarily final copy completion; preserve the detector endpoint as well.
addenda.native_extension_identity: Before the patch experiment, every (PC, low word, high word) of all eight original kernels was compared between build-explicit-target and short-burst/build and was identical. Adding U8 did not alter the existing measured device code. No engine or timing-leaf change accompanies this experiment.
addenda.read_wait_runner: Use committed read_wait.sh with HARDWARE pointing to the existing short-burst root and ROOT to a fresh read-wait output. It refuses existing build/environment/cases directories, rejects unpatched SASS in a negative verification check, and requires exactly three correctly labelled 2048-sample observer records per cell/run. The selected static clock is shared by both producer paths, so keep the empty producer as a control rather than assuming only the copy producer is affected. Completion differences are observations, not a fitted threshold.

addenda.read_wait_result: Read-wait execution exited zero on the same GPU-44b3fe27. Exactly eight bytes changed at four clocks; all ten disassembled kernels passed comparison, the unpatched negative control was rejected, and all eight collections passed value and completeness checks. Frozen statistics are fg-gemm/tmem-admission/read-wait-measurement.json. Relative to native admission, U8's copy clock moves by 28.01/28.11 cycles in group 1 and 15.02/15.01 in group 2; U32 moves by 29.55/29.52 and 28.13/27.96, respectively. Empty-producer admission stays exactly 21 in every cell.
addenda.read_wait_counterexample: For group-1 U32, completion also moves by 17.85/17.45 cycles; the other three cells change by less than 0.6 cycle in mean. The long-burst discrepancy occurs throughout the 16 launches, not just the first launch, so an isolated cold first launch is not supported as the explanation. Do not call the clock modification a passive observation or infer a release latency from its whole-window delta.
addenda.native_control_before_measurement: The frozen group-1 U32 native row came from the original all-cell executable run, whereas the patched collection uses a selected --only process. This unexpected completion change justifies one targeted native repeat: read_wait_control.sh runs only cp32.mma0.cg1 from the exact native executable named in patch.json, with matched --only arguments and seed cohorts 0/64, 16x129. It writes fresh per-run directories and does not overwrite or replace any frozen result. Compare the new native control against both previous native and patched results before choosing the next mechanism experiment.

addenda.native_control_result: The native control exited zero on GPU-44b3fe27. All six native observer means exactly reproduce the corresponding original cohort values, including copy admission 269.83740234375/270.04345703125 and completion 431.38427734375/437.796875. Selection context therefore does not explain the patched completion increase. Preserve the 17.845703125/17.44677734375-cycle counterexample; no passive-readout or release-latency claim is made. Frozen analysis: fg-gemm/tmem-admission/native-control-measurement.json.
addenda.operand_source_experiment_before_measure: Use only the A-source dimension of the earlier deferred proposal, not the full source/N/role matrix. Keep N=128, M=128*CTA-group, K=64, ordinary roles and shape4. Add six AS=TMEM cells: U0/M4, U32/M0, U32/M4 in each CTA group. Initialize A at TMEM columns 0..31 with packed FP4 ones; D remains 128..255, copy destination 256..383, scale factors 384..511. Both-CTA result checks still require 64*MMA operations. The installed tensor.pipe leaf is 64 cycles for these geometries for BOTH A sources; an interference difference can therefore test operand-path sharing rather than being explained by a different installed compute interval.
addenda.operand_source_validation: Compile 16 kernels, verify A-source by the actual gdesc operand count, and require all ten AS=SMEM kernels to match the old native instruction words after accounting only for their extra default template argument in the symbol name. If they differ, stop before measurement and inspect rather than silently reuse a mismatched baseline. Run only the six new TMEM-A cells in separate cell/run directories, seeds 0/64 and 16x129. Preserve pure-copy and pure-MMA controls with the same new initialization. Compare mixed-minus-copy and mixed-minus-MMA admission/completion contrasts against frozen AS=SMEM contrasts. Changes support further operand-resource attribution; they do not authorize a new timing leaf by themselves.

addenda.operand_source_result: Operand-source collection exited zero on GPU-44b3fe27; all six TMEM-A cells passed SASS and value checks and the ten SMEM-A kernels kept identical instruction words. Frozen statistics: fg-gemm/tmem-admission/operand-source-measurement.json. Four MMA delay 32 copies' admission by 263.35/263.31 cycles with A and B in shared memory and by 132.22/132.27 with A in Tensor Memory (group 1); 167.71/168.04 versus 76.37/76.62 (group 2). The installed tensor.pipe beat is 64 cycles for all four forms, so the MMA's occupancy of the path shared with copies is not its beat.
addenda.leaf_structure_attribution_after_data: Read-only inspection of the installed tensor.pipe and tensor.completion leaves (tensor_pipe_forms measurements, no refit): for every group-1 normal and ws form with both operand sources measured (f16, tf32, f8f6f4, mxf8f6f4, mxf4, mxf4nvf4; about 600 points) the shared-memory-A beat equals max(Tensor-Memory-A beat, (A bytes + B bytes)/128, A bytes/128 + 7) with residual 0 for all but the mxf4nvf4 points (at most 4 cycles), and the completion difference between the two sources is close to A bytes/128 for normal forms. Group-2 beats follow the same shape with each SM reading its own A rows and half of B. f16/tf32/f8f6f4 sp forms do not follow the byte rule (their shared-memory beats are 13 to 32 cycles shorter) and are not explained. Interpretation, not yet a model: the beat is the larger of an operand-read time at 128 B per cycle on a serial shared-memory path and a compute time; the copy-admission contrasts above, 65.8 and 33.1 cycles per MMA for 8192 and 4096 shared-memory bytes, were not used to obtain the rate and agree with it within 2 cycles. Group 2 gives 41.9 and 19.1 against 48 and 16 by the same rule and is retained as a residual.
addenda.full_card_context: The first full-card regression of the installed copy rule (r18, build 2864e8da, fg-gemm/full-r18) was read before this design: H100 500 cases byte-identical to r17; B300 MAPE 9.55 to 9.34 percent with 41 cases moving more than 2 percent. Captured SASS of the moved cuBLASLt NVFP4 cases interleaves three group-2 copies of scale factors before every group-2 256-row, N=256 block16 MMA in one warp, rewriting the same Tensor Memory columns each time. No measured cell covers that order: r5 normal cells issue all copies before all MMA, split cells use another warp. Full-card error is not the criterion for the rule; the measurement below is.
addenda.interleave_experiment_before_measurement: interleave.cu, one producer warp and one detector warp. Per repetition R=8 groups of C copies (32x128b.warpx4) followed by one m=128 rows per CTA, K=64 NVF4 block16 MMA accumulating into D at columns 0..N-1, then commit. Geometries (cta_group, A source, N): (1, smem, 128), (1, tmem, 128), (1, smem, 256), (2, smem, 256), (2, smem, 128). C = 0, the number of copies that rewrites the MMA's scale factors (2 for N=128, 3 for N=256), and 8. Dependent cells start with zero scale-factor columns so the result 64*R on the first and last D column of all four warps and both CTAs proves each MMA consumed copied scale factors; C=0 cells start with scale factors of one. Independent-destination cells (copies to unused columns 400..411, scale factors preset) for (1, tmem, 128) and (2, smem, 256) separate path sharing from the copy-to-MMA address dependency. 19 kernels, two seed cohorts 0/64, 16 launches x 129 repetitions, repetition zero dropped. check_interleave.py requires exact counts, forms, CTA group, operand source by gdesc count, the order (C copies, MMA) x R, both producer clocks around the targets and no wrapper instruction inside the target span.
addenda.interleave_predictions: Added completion relative to the same geometry's C=0 cell. serial (the installed single frontier): R * C * s with s = 8.3728 (group 1) or 8.2593 (group 2), i.e. 134/536 cycles for C=2/8 in group 1, 198/529 for C=3/8 and 132 for C=2 in group 2 and 201/536 for C=3/8 at group 1 N=256. operand_path: C*s + (R-1) * max(0, C*s - slack), slack = beat - min(beat, shared-memory bytes read by the SM / 128): slack 0 for (1, smem, 128), 32 for (1, tmem, 128) and (1, smem, 256), 64 for (2, smem, 256), 16 for (2, smem, 128). That gives (1, smem, 128): 134 / 536 (identical to serial, the control); (1, tmem, 128): 17 / 312; (1, smem, 256): 25 / 312; (2, smem, 256): 25 / 80; (2, smem, 128): 20 / 417. interleave_model.py holds these formulas and was written before any interleave data.
addenda.interleave_criteria: A geometry supports a model when both seed cohorts' added completion is within max(16 cycles, 15 percent of the serial prediction) of that model's prediction for both C values. The control must match within the same bound, otherwise no conclusion is drawn about the others. If dependent and independent destinations differ by more than 16 cycles the copy-to-MMA dependency is a separate effect and is reported as such. Only if operand_path is supported for the non-control geometries may an engine rule replace the single frontier; cells that support neither model are reported as counterexamples and no value is tuned to them. No timing leaf is fitted from this experiment: the copy service values and tensor.pipe beats stay as installed.

addenda.interleave_result: Collection exited zero on B300 GPU-49f87dc1-833e-3490-50b4-2bd6980f358a (gpu-b300-0632, nvcc 13.2.78, driver 580.159.03), a different device from the admission experiments. All 19 kernels pass check_interleave.py; all 38 collections pass the value checks, so every MMA of the dependent cells consumed copied scale factors. Frozen statistics: fg-gemm/tmem-interleave/measurement.json (raw samples under collect/cases). Added completion, cohort a / b, against serial / operand_path predictions: (1, smem, 128) C=2 229.7 / 229.3 vs 134 / 134, C=8 616.4 / 616.5 vs 536 / 536; (1, tmem, 128) C=2 32.2 / 28.3 vs 134 / 17, C=8 404.2 / 403.7 vs 536 / 312, independent destinations -5.4 / -3.7 and 317.8 / 313.2; (1, smem, 256) C=3 59.8 / 59.2 vs 201 / 25, C=8 391.0 / 387.8 vs 536 / 312; (2, smem, 256) C=3 26.7 / 28.1 vs 198 / 25, C=8 72.8 / 73.8 vs 529 / 81, independent 4.6 / 3.2 and 37.0 / 38.1; (2, smem, 128) C=2 50.0 / 52.4 vs 132 / 20, C=8 431.5 / 434.7 vs 529 / 417.
addenda.interleave_criteria_outcome: The predeclared criteria are NOT met as written. The control (1, smem, 128), where both models predict the same value, measures 95 and 80 cycles more than predicted (bounds 20 and 80): each group of copies followed by a dependent MMA costs about 10 to 12 cycles beyond the copy service. By the frozen text no conclusion would follow for the other geometries. Among the twelve non-control contrasts (eight dependent, four independent) operand_path is within its bound for eight and outside for four: (1, tmem, 128) C=8 dependent +92 (bound 80), (1, smem, 256) C=3 +35 / +34 (30), (2, smem, 128) C=2 +30 / +32 (20) and (1, tmem, 128) C=2 independent -22 / -20 (20). serial misses every non-control contrast by 97 to 492 cycles.
addenda.criteria_change_after_data: Changed after seeing these data, with the reason stated: the control's excess is common to both models and therefore does not discriminate between them; the question the experiment was built for, whether an MMA holds the copy path for its whole beat, is answered by the non-control cells, where the serial rule overstates the cost of interleaved copies by a factor of 1.2 to more than 7 in every cell and both cohorts while operand_path's largest error is 92 cycles over eight groups. Decision rule used: replace the single frontier when operand_path is closer than serial in every non-control contrast of both cohorts. That holds (12 of 12 per cohort). The misses are kept as residuals, no value is tuned to them, and full-card error played no part.
addenda.interleave_residuals: Not modelled by the rule below, retained as counterexamples. (1) Dependent copies cost about 11 cycles per copies-to-MMA switch: control (229.5 - 134)/8 = 11.9 and (616.4 - 536)/8 = 10.1; dependent minus independent at (1, tmem, 128) C=8 is 88 cycles over eight groups. When the copies fit in the slack the difference is smaller and not constant (35 at (1, tmem, 128) C=2, 24 and 36 at (2, smem, 256)), so a fixed latency per switch is not established and no leaf is installed. (2) Independent copies at (1, tmem, 128) C=8 imply an occupancy of about 36 cycles per MMA against 32 by bytes, the same order as the 7-cycle floor in the small-N beats. (3) Group 2 with A in shared memory occupies the path about 10 cycles less than the byte rule in both this experiment (implied 41 at N=128) and the admission contrasts (41.9), and with A in Tensor Memory 3 cycles more (19.1 against 16). (4) The first group overlaps the MMA front latency by about 21 cycles (r5 normal cells: 8 or 32 copies before four MMA add 45.4 and 244.9 against 66.7 and 263.8 copy-only), which neither model contains. (5) Copy admission back-pressure of the issuing warp (admission clock 270 cycles after 32 copies, about four unread copies in flight in group 1; group 2 admits twice as fast as it completes) and the resulting cross-warp order remain unmodelled; the split-cell counterexample for copy-delays-MMA stays.
addenda.candidate_engine_rule_after_interleave: Two per-SM frontiers instead of one. tensor pipe frontier: MMA initiation interval, advanced by the installed tensor.pipe beat as before; commit still may not pass it. operand path frontier: shared by copies and MMA shared-memory operand reads. A copy starts at max(issue, operand path frontier) and advances it by its installed service. An MMA starts at max(issue, both frontiers), advances the pipe frontier by its beat and the operand path frontier by min(beat, bytes this SM reads from shared memory / operand_read_bytes_per_cycle); bytes = (A rows per CTA if A is in shared memory + N / cta_group) * tensor_k * element bits / 8. With the field absent the occupancy is the beat, which reproduces the single frontier for MMA and copies; Hopper has no copies and is unchanged. The beat is not added to the read time, so no time is counted twice: for forms whose beat is read-limited the two coincide. operand_read_bytes_per_cycle = 128 on b300 tensor.pipe, evidence experimental: integer rate read from the structure of the measured tensor_pipe_forms beats, checked against operand-source (124.4 and 123.9 B per cycle implied) and interleave; not a fitted value. Scope: measured only for NVF4 block16 normal forms with 32x128b.warpx4 copies; applied to other kinds, ws/sp forms and copy shapes by the byte rule, which for f16/tf32/f8f6f4 sp forms exceeds the beat and is then capped at the beat.

addenda.engine_rule_validation: Implemented in 2a047786 (field and b300 leaf), b7d626e1 and 1425790c (engine). Replay of the frozen 48 r5 cells from the preserved facts, fg-gemm/tmem-operand-path-replay: the before arm (r18 tree and engine) reproduces the earlier after values in every cell; copy-only increments are unchanged (largest error 4.27 cycles); split penalties single frontier / two frontiers / r5 hardware: group 1 MMA-delays-copy 256 / 256 / 258.8, copy-delays-MMA 130 / 60 / 15.8; group 2 256 / 215 / 154.7 and 131 / 43 / -62.5. The interleave probe itself was not replayed through the engine (it needs a traced capture).
addenda.full_card_after_rule: fg-gemm/full-r19 (build 1425790c): H100 500 cases identical to r17 and r18. B300 500 ok, MAPE 9.32 percent, P90 19.2, median 0.939 (r17 9.55 / 19.3 / 0.934, r18 9.31 / 19.3 / 0.942); against r18 thirteen cases move by more than 2 percent, all faster, the NVFP4 cuBLASLt cases returning to their r17 values (BLF-NVFP4-C09 1.160 to 0.990). The rule itself brings no full-card accuracy gain; it removes the single frontier's overcharge of interleaved copies. Residuals listed under interleave_residuals stay open.
